name: Sanballat
bio: Sanballat the Horonite was furious when he heard Nehemiah had come to seek Israel's welfare, and later mocked the Jews with Tobiah and Geshem the Arab as rebels against the king when they began rebuilding Jerusalem's wall. Nehemiah told them God would prosper the work and that they had no share, right, or claim in Jerusalem (Nehemiah 2:10, 19-20). His continued opposition is told in detail in the chapters ahead. When the Jews kept building despite his mockery, Sanballat joined other peoples in conspiring to attack Jerusalem and halt the work, a plot Nehemiah foiled by posting an armed watch (Nehemiah 4:1-15). As the wall neared completion, Sanballat repeatedly tried to lure Nehemiah away to harm him, then sent an open letter accusing him of plotting rebellion, hoping to frighten him into stopping the work. He also hired Shemaiah son of Delaiah and the prophetess Noadiah to intimidate Nehemiah, all without success; the wall was finished in fifty-two days despite him (Nehemiah 6:1-16).
